Tidy posterior summaries

Source: R/tidiers.R
tidy.Rd

Summarise saved posterior draws in a tibble, without refitting or drawing new samples. These methods also work with broom::tidy().

Usage

tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdpbinomial'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdpnormal'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bdplm'
tidy(
  x,
  conf.int = FALSE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  effects = c("coefficients", "sigma"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bdpsurvival'
tidy(
  x,
  conf.int = FALSE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  time = x$args1$surv_time,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted bdpbinomial, bdpnormal, bdplm, or bdpsurvival object. Fits from bdplogit() use class bdplm.

...

Additional arguments are not supported and produce an error.

conf.int

Logical; include equal-tailed credible limits? Defaults to FALSE.

conf.level

Credible interval probability, strictly between zero and one. Defaults to 0.95.

exponentiate

Logical; exponentiate logistic coefficients or the two-arm survival effect? Defaults to FALSE. Not supported for other quantities.

effects

For regression fits, "coefficients" returns the intercept, treatment effect, and covariate coefficients; "sigma" returns the residual SD of a linear model. Logistic fits have no residual SD parameter.

time

For a one-arm survival fit, a single finite, nonnegative time at which to summarise survival. Defaults to the fit's surv_time. Cannot be supplied for a two-arm fit.

Value

A tibble with one row per quantity and columns term, estimate, and std.error. Despite its conventional name, std.error is a posterior SD, not a frequentist standard error or Monte Carlo standard error. If conf.int = TRUE, conf.low and conf.high contain equal-tailed credible limits, computed using stats::quantile() with its default interpolation. Survival results also contain time. Results retain full numerical precision. No test statistics or p-values are reported.

Details

Binomial and normal fits return treatment, then control and difference when a control arm is present. These describe event probabilities or population means, and the treatment-minus-control difference. Estimates are posterior medians. Differences are calculated from paired draws, including when controls are historical only or the fit used compare = FALSE.

Regression fits return posterior means on the original covariate scale, with the intercept named (Intercept). Logistic coefficients are on the log-odds scale unless exponentiate = TRUE.

One-arm survival fits return a survival row containing the posterior median survival probability and a time column. Two-arm fits return a treatment row for the approximate common log hazard ratio, treatment relative to control, with time = NA. Its estimate is the posterior mean of the inverse-variance-weighted interval log hazard ratio draws used by summary(); it is not a time-specific hazard ratio or an assumption of proportional hazards.

With exponentiate = TRUE, the estimate is the exponential of the posterior mean log effect, not the posterior mean odds ratio or hazard ratio. Credible limits are exponentiated log-scale quantiles. The std.error column is the SD of the exponentiated draws, so it is on the reported ratio scale, not the log scale or a delta-method approximation. For an exponentiated logistic intercept, the estimate describes baseline odds.

See also

glance, summary

Author

Graeme L. Hickey

Examples

set.seed(42)
fit <- bdpbinomial(y_t = 8, N_t = 40, y_c = 5, N_c = 40,
  y0_t = 10, N0_t = 50, y0_c = 8, N0_c = 50,
  method = "fixed", number_mcmc = 1000)
tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   term       estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>         <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 treatment    0.204     0.0425   0.127      0.293
#> 2 control      0.147     0.0415   0.0759     0.234
#> 3 difference   0.0555    0.0591  -0.0681     0.179
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>    nobs n.historical n.draws alpha.treatment alpha.control
#>   <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>           <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1    80          100    1000           0.998         0.676
